dod_intent_evidence: Defense-contract-adjacent news coverage (defence-blog.com, 2026-07-18: 'Pittsburgh startup pitches EV kit to elite troops'; second outlet: 'Why Special Operations Forces Want This New Pittsburgh Electric [Vehicle Kit]... the company recently demonstrated its new system') plus an investor's own announcement naming the company 'dual-use military/civilian' — see News section. No DoD/military language appears anywhere on the company's own site.
score_evidence: '165 horsepower / 120 kW...Instant torque and control...Experience the EPIC APEX of UTV performance' → lab_language_intensity (pure consumer performance-spec bragging, zero operational framing, despite reported special-operations demo)

'Fast-charge compatible: At home or on the go using existing EV charging stations' and full technical-spec tables (voltage, battery, charging standard J1772) with zero mention of DDIL/ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR/SWaP-C anywhere in ~1,332 words → deployment_awareness_absence

'Enjoy the future as you take a ride in your new electric UTV' — every page addresses a recreational buyer/rider; zero mention of operators, warfighters, training, or CONOPS anywhere in the pack → operator_absence

'Delivers Q2 2027' / 'Alpha Deliveries Q3 2026' pre-order stage, 5-person team, fresh 2025 VC investment (Uma Ventures) — tiny team racing a hardware delivery timeline while reportedly courting special operations customers → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Charge anywhere...at home or on the go using existing EV charging stations' assumes grid/charging-station access
blind_spots.operator_reality: The reported use case (special operations infiltrating behind enemy lines) is definitionally DDIL — no J1772 charging station exists in a denied area; there's no mention of field charging, generator compatibility, or battery-swap logistics for an extended patrol, the SWaP-C analog to the 30fps crowd-detection failure
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product and go-to-market were built entirely around the civilian recreational off-road buyer (Shopify storefront, pre-order deposits, garage charging)
blind_spots.evidence_quote: fast-charge compatible: At home or on the go using existing EV charging stations

blind_spots.blind_spot: Built on an off-the-shelf civilian donor chassis (Polaris RZR XP1000) and consumer components (NOCO 12V battery) with no ruggedization or acoustic/thermal signature discussion
blind_spots.operator_reality: The news coverage's own framing is that stealth (low acoustic signature) is the entire value proposition for special-operations customers, yet nothing in the company's own language addresses signature management, MIL-STD shock/vibration/dust testing, or combat durability beyond consumer off-roading
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Engineering effort visibly went into powertrain performance (165 HP, instant torque) for the recreational buyer, not survivability engineering for a tactical vehicle
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Based on the versatile and capable Polaris Rzr chassis, the SPM EPEX delivers performance that you didn't know you needed

blind_spots.blind_spot: Battery (183 lbs) and vehicle weight (1,500 lbs) specs are framed purely around recreational range ('Ride all day, charge in your garage overnight') with no SWaP-C tradeoff discussion
blind_spots.operator_reality: A special-operations customer needs to know sling-load and internal-airlift weight/dimension limits (e.g. CH-47/C-130 constraints) for insertion — a fundamentally different design constraint than trailer-hauling a UTV to a trailhead, and nothing in the pack shows this tradeoff being engineered for
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Spec sheet was written to sell a $40-45K premium recreational vehicle, not to pass a military airlift-compatibility requirement
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Vehicle Weight | 1,500 lbs...Est Range (20 kWh) | 50-60 miles

opener_hook: SPM demoed its electric UTV powertrain to special operations forces (Defence Blog, July 2026) while every public spec sheet is still framed around garage charging and weekend trail riding — is a signature-managed, airlift-rated variant on the roadmap?
what_they_do: Builds high-performance electric UTV powertrains and turnkey vehicles (EPEX, EVK conversion kit) sold as consumer recreational off-road products, with reported demos to special operations forces as a dual-use military application.
